## Citing depictr

If you use depictr in published work, please cite it.

> Bernabeu, P. (2026). depictr: A unified toolkit for visualising statistical
> models and data. R package version `r packageVersion("depictr")`.
> Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN).
> <https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.depictr>

```{r bibtex, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
# Build the BibTeX entry from the installed version so it never drifts, then
# render it with a copy button and a download link. The button uses the
# browser clipboard API; the link is a self-contained data URI, so neither
# depends on a static file being shipped alongside the site.
ver <- as.character(utils::packageVersion("depictr"))
bib <- paste(
  "@Manual{depictr,",
  "  title  = {{depictr}: A unified toolkit for visualising statistical models and data},",
  "  author = {Pablo Bernabeu},",
  "  year   = {2026},",
  "  publisher = {Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN)},",
  sprintf("  note   = {R package version %s},", ver),
  "  doi    = {10.32614/CRAN.package.depictr},",
  "  url    = {https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=depictr},",
  "}",
  sep = "\n"
)
esc <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
}
uri <- paste0(
  "data:application/x-bibtex;charset=utf-8,",
  utils::URLencode(bib, reserved = TRUE)
)
cat(sprintf(
'<div class="citation-bibtex">
<pre id="depictr-bibtex"><code>%s</code></pre>
<p class="citation-bibtex-actions">
<button type="button" class="btn btn-primary btn-sm" onclick="depictrCopyBibtex(this)">Copy BibTeX</button>
<a class="btn btn-outline-primary btn-sm" download="depictr.bib" href="%s">Download .bib</a>
</p>
</div>
<script>
function depictrCopyBibtex(btn) {
  var code = document.getElementById("depictr-bibtex");
  navigator.clipboard.writeText(code.innerText).then(function () {
    var label = btn.textContent;
    btn.textContent = "Copied";
    setTimeout(function () { btn.textContent = label; }, 1500);
  });
}
</script>
', esc(bib), uri))
```

R users can also retrieve this citation directly with `citation("depictr")`.

## The developer

depictr is developed by Pablo Bernabeu, a researcher in the Department of
Education at the University of Oxford. His work spans cognitive psychology and
neuroscience, linguistics, education and digital technologies, drawing on a
range of methods that include behavioural and EEG experiments, corpus analysis
and computational modelling. He is a Fellow of the Software Sustainability
Institute (2020), recognised for his work on R-based tools for data
presentation, and holds a PhD in Psychology from Lancaster University.

More about his work is on [his website](https://pablobernabeu.github.io),
on [GitHub](https://github.com/pablobernabeu) and via
[ORCID 0000-0003-1083-2460](https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1083-2460).

A sibling [Python package](https://pablobernabeu.github.io/depictr-py/),
available on PyPI, shares the same design.

## Licence

depictr is released under the [MIT licence](../LICENSE.html), a short
permissive licence that allows use, modification and redistribution in both
open and closed projects, provided the copyright notice is retained. The full
text is on the site's licence page.

## Versioning and archival

CRAN assigned the package the DOI
<https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.depictr>
on publication. It names the package across all its versions, so the version
in the citation identifies the release used. Releases are also tagged on
[GitHub](https://github.com/pablobernabeu/depictr/releases) and archived on
Zenodo, where the concept DOI
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21266308> resolves to
the latest archived release and each release has a DOI of its own. What changed
in each release is recorded in the [changelog](../news/index.html).

## Contributing and support

Bugs and feature requests are best reported on the
[GitHub issues page](https://github.com/pablobernabeu/depictr/issues), ideally
with a small reproducible example. The [contributing guide](../CONTRIBUTING.html)
explains how to set up for development and what to check before opening a pull
request.
